My Dear Ivor!

You realise of course that it is utterly impossible for me to answer all your letters as they should be answered; lack of space does not allow me to go into details. I promise I shall save up all I have to say for later. All I can do at present is to thank you for being such a good friend. I received the parcel yesterday and your letter from 25th Oct., today. Thanks for the dedication to me. I like your poem but I am afraid it will be too long to be printed, at any rate, save it for later. Old Daley is now stabled in "HQ". I had no opportunity of seeing him. I met a chap who has been in the Attlee Brigade in Spain and knows the Glasgow Comrades. Give Bill my regards. He has written so far five letters and got no reply from me. Two letters which I wrote are, I assume, filling the files of the Special Branch. Ethel Mannin has also never received my letters in which I thanked her for the books she sent me and explained to her my personal views on violence, etc. Please tell her that her "Privileged Spectator" was stolen from my cell and could not be found in spite of the whole prison being searched. Isn't she also speaking at the Holborn meeting? I've been waiting to have a word from Phil but he - I take it - is extremely busy just now. Tell him that I am well. From my point of view, my imprisonment is the best Service reaction could do us, the longer it lasts the more profitable for our cause, if fully exploited for propaganda. I personally am well pleased, for with my being kept behind bars the counter revolutionary forces establish beyond doubt a revolutionary alibi for me, which will be recognised in Europe and, through the propaganda of the "I.W." and "L'Admata" in the States and Spain, the imprisonment of Max Holtz and Erich Mishsamm in Germany made their cause known in the whole political world. It will be clear to the revolutionaries who have escaped Nazi and bolshevist persecution as well as to the new generation that we had nothing in common with the corrupted lot of refugee politicians who became agents for the Allies. I disagree with the London Intellectuals who, headed by Herbert Read, Ethel, etc., recently stated "the revolutionary situation we were expecting has not and may not at all come". Tell them to study Lenin's explanation of a revolutionary situation or better still Bakinson's letter to and Kropotkins writings "a la revolt"!. War Com pointed out that Haley had a revolution when all other left papers here still unaware of the fact. The Alien and German soldiers did exactly what the German soldiers did 1917, they voted with their feet against the war. We were the first in this country to state the facts that the war had been perverted into a deliberate attempt to liquidate all revolutionary elements in Europe. After the events in Greece everybody else repeated our statement. The strikes in U.S.A. and this country indicate the return of the militant sections of the working class to rev. tradition and the re adoption of the principles deserted by the Marxists since 1913, namely; International solidarity and Social Revolution. The tendency is clearly against party bureaucracy and pseudo-socialism for direct action and syndicalists methods. I am watching with particular interest the tactics of our Labour government. The very same as the S.P.D. policy in Germany! Hit the left and work into the hands of the counter-rev. the R.C.P. is being accused of having financed the dockers strike! That's just what the reaction is waiting for, re-birth of the Communist bpgey which gives the Right a justification to build up, legally, or illegally, a strong counter-revolutionary force. Discredit the striking workers and the middle class will refuse its support to the cause of the workers and swing right turn. Tell the I.L.P. Comrades (and, if you have a chance, old Lasky), the dis-illusionment in the Civil Prisons and D.B's is increasing. No amnesty from a Labour Government is about the greatest political failure. (Even the arch-counter revolutionary Napoleon issued amnesties on different occasions). Hardly anybody in Prison and D.B. has voted for the election, of the local governments and the saying spreads "Labour politicians are as bad as the Conservatories!"

Passing regards to all the Comrades.

P.S. Please ask M.L. if she has my letter written last week-end.
